sentences.text: Erlikosaurus was a small therizinosaurid estimated to reach about 3.4 meters in length.
This animal possessed a well-developed beak and toothed jaws adapted for a herbivorous diet.
Its skull featured a moderately elongated snout with a premaxilla featuring elongated nasal processes.
The holotype skull of Erlikosaurus measures approximately 25 cm in length.
Erlikosaurus had four toes on its feet, with the first toe articulated to the ankle.
The preserved left humerus was robust, had an estimated length of 30 cm, and featured an elongated epiphysis and a large deltoidal process.
The animal possessed very symmetrical teeth with moderate denticles.
The name Erlikosaurus combines the Turko-Mongolian demon king Erlik with the Greek word for lizard.
The species name andrewsi honors the American paleontologist Roy Chapman Andrews.
CT scans of the holotype skull revealed that Erlikosaurus had well-developed senses of smell, hearing, and balance.
Bite force measurements showed a range of 43–65 N at the snout tip and 90–134 N at the last maxillary tooth region.
Researchers concluded that the keratinous beak enhanced skull stability by reducing susceptibility to bending during feeding.
Fossils of Erlikosaurus were discovered in the Bayan Shireh Formation of Mongolia in 1972.
The Erlikosaurus fossils were found during a Soviet-Mongolian expedition in the Ömnögovi Province in 1972.
The holotype specimen of Erlikosaurus was found at the Bayshin Tsav locality within the Bayan Shireh Formation.
The genus Erlikosaurus was described by Barsbold and Perle in 1980.
Therizinosaurs like Erlikosaurus were theropods that ate plants and possessed a backward-facing pubis similar to ornithischians.
Erlikosaurus likely used a leaf-stripping feeding method involving active beak use aided by its neck.
Evidence suggests Erlikosaurus used the tip of its snout to reach for soft foliage or fruits rather than active mastication.
Researchers suggest Erlikosaurus was aided by a down-turned tip of the lower jaws, symphyseal regions, and stress-mitigating beaks.
Gregory S. Paul hypothesized that the long, slender claws of Erlikosaurus were used for self-defense.
Differences between Erlikosaurus and the co-existing Segnosaurus suggest they occupied different ecological niches.
Erlikosaurus belongs to the parent group Therizinosauria.
Erlikosaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
Perle originally assigned Erlikosaurus to the Segnosauridae, a group now known as Therizinosauridae, a classification confirmed by later cladistic analyses.
Erlikosaurus lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period.
The Bayan Shireh Formation, where Erlikosaurus was found, dates from approximately 95.9 to 89.6 million years ago (Cenomanian to Santonian stages).
Sediment analysis indicates Erlikosaurus lived in a semi-arid climate featuring wet environments with large meandering rivers and lakes.
Erlikosaurus lived from the Turonian to the Santonian stages, between 93.9 and 83.6 million years ago.
Erlikosaurus lived alongside the larger therizinosaurid Segnosaurus in the Bayan Shireh Formation.
In 2010, Gregory S. Paul suggested that Erlikosaurus might be synonymous with Enigmosaurus, a hypothesis disputed by Rinchen Barsbold.
Most paleontologists currently consider Enigmosaurus and Erlikosaurus to be separate genera.
In 1970, Rozhdestvensky proposed that therizinosaurs were theropods rather than non-dinosaur creatures, a view that was debated before being widely accepted.
